pages.text: Both are thin pillars that connect $(item)only at their two ends$(), along the axis they are placed on. They are good for long straight runs and handle up to $(item)10,000 V$(). Placed inside liquid concrete, they dry into a $(item)concrete encased$() version, perfect for burying a line in a floor or a wall.

$(l)Copycat cable block$()$(br)Connects on $(item)all six faces$(), like a cable hub, but takes the look of any block you apply to it, in the same way as Create's copycat blocks. Use it to hide wiring inside a building. It keeps the standard $(item)1,000 V$() limit.

$(l)Diagonal cable block$()$(br)Links one side face with the face $(item)above$() or $(item)below$() it, so a line can climb a slope or a staircase without a stack of hubs. It handles up to $(item)100,000 V$().
None of these has a current limit: only cable hubs burn out from too much current.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
